name: Plotting Market Data
description: Draw clear, honest charts of prices, returns and drawdowns.

lessonNames.l2-readable: A chart someone else can read
lessonNames.l9-log-axis: When to use a log axis
lessonNames.l13-exit-project: Returns, volatility and drawdown from a CSV

lessonObjectives.l1-figure-and-axes: Make a line chart with matplotlib’s figure and axes objects.
lessonObjectives.l2-readable: Label axes, units and series directly.
lessonObjectives.l3-price-chart: Plot prices against dates with a readable date axis.
lessonObjectives.l4-rebasing: Compare two price series by rebasing both to 100.
lessonObjectives.l5-returns-chart: Plot daily returns and spot volatility clustering.
lessonObjectives.l6-shape-of-returns: Draw a histogram of returns and compare it with a normal curve.
lessonObjectives.l7-drawing-drawdown: Plot the running peak and the drawdown beneath it.
lessonObjectives.l8-vol-over-time: Plot annualised rolling volatility and read its regimes.
lessonObjectives.l9-log-axis: Choose between a linear and a log price axis for a long history.
lessonObjectives.l10-panels: Lay out price, returns and drawdown as aligned panels.
lessonObjectives.l11-two-variables: Plot one return series against another and read the relationship.
lessonObjectives.l12-charts-that-mislead: Spot truncated axes and cherry-picked windows, and fix them.
lessonObjectives.l13-exit-project: Build the 1.1 exit project: one script from a price file to three charts.
